chief_complaint: chalk-white patches around eyes and knuckles
hpi_details: A 50-year-old female presents to the clinic with chalk-white patches around eyes and knuckles. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she has a severe nutritional deficiency or a skin fungus that is bleaching the pigment out of her skin.
concerns: She is worried that the white patches will continue spreading over her face and hands until people begin staring at her in public.
expectations: She hopes to get blood tests to check for vitamin deficiencies and a cream to bring her natural skin color back.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Vitiligo is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Vitiligo: Topical Tacrolimus, narrow-band UVB phototherapy, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Vitiligo.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Tinea versicolor without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Rapidly progressive, widespread depigmentation — screen for associated autoimmune thyroid disease or Addison disease.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Autoimmune destruction of melanocytes causing chalk-white depigmented patches around the eyes and knuckles.
red_flags: Rapidly progressive, widespread depigmentation — screen for associated autoimmune thyroid disease or Addison disease
Symptoms of coexisting autoimmune disease (fatigue, weight change, palpitations) — vitiligo clusters with autoimmune thyroiditis
Ocular or auditory symptoms (tinnitus, hearing loss, uveitis) — consider Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada syndrome

must_ask.say: Where are the patches — around your eyes, knuckles?
Does vitiligo run in your family?
How does this affect you emotionally?

history.answer: I noticed chalk-white patches developing around my eyes and over my knuckles, and they have been gradually spreading.
They started about two months ago around my eyelids and knuckles and have been slowly enlarging and becoming more obvious.
They are mostly around both eyes and over the joints on the back of my fingers on both hands.
They are completely milky white and flat with distinct edges, not raised, and there is no flaking or crusting.
No, they do not itch, hurt, or burn at all.
No, they stay there constantly once they appear; they do not come and go or fade away like hives.
I have been feeling quite fatigued and run down lately, but I have not had any fever, chills, or body aches.
I have never had white patches like this before, and I have never received treatment for a skin condition.
No, my lips, mouth, eyes, and private areas do not have any sores, ulcers, or redness.
No, my skin is not peeling, blistering, or tender, and I do not have any purple spots.
No, I have had no swelling of my lips or face, no difficulty breathing, and no throat tightness or dizziness.
I have not started any new prescription drugs, antibiotics, gout medication, pain relievers, or supplements.
No, I have not changed my cosmetics, soaps, detergents, or jewelry, and I have not handled any unusual plants or chemicals.
No, I have not had any insect bites, I haven't been hiking, and I haven't traveled or used public saunas recently.
No, I do not have asthma, atopic dermatitis, eczema, or allergic rhinitis.
No, there was no cut, sunburn, rash, or injury in those spots before the white patches showed up.
My finger joints feel completely fine with no pain or stiffness, and my nails look completely normal.
I tried putting on an over-the-counter moisturizer, but it didn't change the spots at all; I haven't used steroid or antifungal creams.
No, I have not had any palpitations, heat or cold intolerance, tremors, or unexpected weight changes.
No, I have not had any vision changes, eye pain, ringing in my ears, or hearing difficulty.
I have been happily married for over twenty years with only my husband, and neither of us has ever had genital sores or ulcers.
I wondered if I have a severe vitamin deficiency or if I picked up a fungus that's bleaching the color out of my skin.
I'm terrified that these white spots will keep spreading across my whole face and hands until people start staring at me in public.
It makes me very self-conscious when meeting people, especially because the patches around my eyes are so visible.
I hope you can run some blood tests to see what nutrients I'm lacking and give me a cream to bring my normal color back.
I have been healthy all my life with no high blood pressure, diabetes, or autoimmune disorders.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or vitamins.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or anything else.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only drink a glass of wine on social occasions once or twice a month.
I work in an office as an administrator, and I live with my husband and two college-aged children.
My mother has Hashimoto's thyroiditis, but no one in my family has had vitiligo or white patches.
My last period was three weeks ago; my cycles have become slightly irregular over the past year, and there is no chance of pregnancy.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.6°C.
Well-appearing, alert female in no acute distress.
Well-demarcated, depigmented chalk-white macules and patches around bilateral periorbital areas and overlying the dorsal knuckles; lesions are flat without erythema, scale, atrophy, or induration.
Sclerae anicteric, conjunctivae pink without pallor, injection, or uveitic signs.
Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light; extraocular movements intact without pain or visual disturbance.
Oral mucosa moist and pink without depigmented lesions, ulcers, or erosions.
No cervical, submandibular, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy palpated.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, smooth, symmetric, and non-tender, with no palpable nodules.
Bilateral proximal and distal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints show full range of motion without swelling, erythema, tenderness, or nail dystrophy.
